note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.text: The valley that flows with the discharge of the people of the Fire, for everyone who slanders people and defames them.

The word means the one who criticises people and reviles them. The commentators differed over the two words: some say the backbiter is the one who eats the flesh of people, some the other way round, and some say the first mocks to the face and the second behind the back.
Some said a particular man is meant, and Tabari settles it: the words reach everyone who slanders, whoever he is.
He gathered wealth and did not spend it in the way of God, and did not pay the right of God that was due upon it, but gathered it and stored it away and hoarded it.
He counted it meticulously and kept track of it. The reciters differ over the reading, and Tabari says both ways of reading the first word are correct and close in meaning.

phrases.translation: thinking that their wealth will make them immortal
phrases.text: He thinks the wealth he gathered and counted, and was too miserly to spend, will keep him in this world and hold death off from him.
It is not so, as he supposed. His wealth will not make him immortal, and he will perish for his deeds.

phrases.translation: Such a person will certainly be tossed into the Crusher
phrases.text: On the day of resurrection he will be cast into al-Hutama, one of the names of the Fire, and the name means the one that crushes everything thrown into it.

phrases.translation: And what will make you realize what the Crusher is
phrases.text: What has made you know, O Muhammad, what al-Hutama is.
Then He tells him what it is: the Fire whose pain and heat reach the hearts.
The same sense again, the Fire that mounts up over the hearts.

phrases.translation: It will be sealed over them
phrases.text: The Fire is shut over these mockers and slanderers, hermetically sealed. The commentators agree on the sense of the word, and Ibn Zayd explains it from the Arabs: he closed the door.
